decided.question: what sortOrder the up and down controls send, given that a move is one PATCH of one row
decided.chose: up sends the sortOrder of the row above minus one and down sends the sortOrder of the row below plus one, so the moved row lands strictly past the neighbour it moved over and the list comes back reordered; a value outside 0-32767 is clamped to the bound
decided.rejected: sending the neighbour's own value, which leaves the two rows tied on sortOrder and the name tiebreak of REQ-02-009 deciding the order, so a press can leave the list exactly as it was
decided.why: rule 3 — the reading whose effect is visible and cannot be mistaken for a dropped write; the rejected one is a silent no-op, and the swap that would avoid both is foreclosed by the single-PATCH rule the spec already states
decided.recordedAt: the contracts' Screens section, the paragraph under the Settings mock, as a Decided note beside the ordering rule; the consequence is carried into Known Gaps row 5 of 02-request-topics.md (repeated moves into one gap can close it and leave two rows sharing a value) and observed by TC-02-E2E-01, which presses up on the third staff row and reads the order back
